identification.summary: UNK_AcademicFlare is Proofpoint's temporary designation for a suspected Russia-aligned cluster that uses device code phishing against Microsoft 365 accounts. It begins with outreach from compromised government and military email accounts, builds rapport around the target's expertise, then proposes a meeting or interview and shares a document link [S2][S3]. The link leads to a Cloudflare Worker page that imitates a OneDrive share and walks the victim into entering a code on Microsoft's genuine device login page, which gives the attacker an access token for the account [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: 2025-09 (Proofpoint has tracked the activity since September 2025, per press coverage) [S2]
identification.notes: The 'UNK_' prefix marks an unattributed, uncategorized Proofpoint cluster [S1][S2]. The same Proofpoint report covers the criminal group TA2723, which uses salary-themed lures and the Graphish and SquarePhish tooling; this is a separate cluster and its facts are not merged here [S2][S3]. No Microsoft-assigned name was found in the sources reviewed.

attribution.confidence: Low. Proofpoint assesses the cluster as suspected or likely Russia-aligned; no government attribution or named sponsoring organization was found [S2].
attribution.basis: Proofpoint's stated reasoning is the focus on Russia-focused specialists at think tanks and on Ukrainian government and energy organizations [S2].

objectives: Account takeover of Microsoft 365 mailboxes and data of government, think tank, and academic targets. Proofpoint's reasoning for Russia alignment implies an intelligence-collection interest in Russia and Ukraine topics, but the sources reviewed do not state objectives explicitly [S2].

targeting.notes: Lures are Russia and Ukraine themed, and the cluster targets Russia-focused specialists [S2][S3]. Initial contact comes from compromised government and military accounts [S2].

capabilities.summary: The cluster abuses the legitimate OAuth device authorization flow, so no software vulnerability is exploited [S2]. Its tradecraft is rapport-building email from compromised government and military accounts, a OneDrive-spoofing page hosted on a Cloudflare Worker, and a prompt for the victim to enter a code on Microsoft's real device login page [S2][S3]. Validation of the code gives the actor access tokens to the victim's Microsoft 365 account [S2]. Proofpoint advises blocking device code flows through Conditional Access where possible, per press coverage [S2]. The sources reviewed do not name custom malware or the specific phishing kit used by this cluster.

campaigns.name: Start of tracked device code phishing activity
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reports tracking this cluster's activity from September 2025 onward, including compromised-account outreach to think tank and government-linked targets [S2].

campaigns.name: Proofpoint public reporting
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint published 'Access granted: phishing with device code authorization for account takeover', which describes the cluster; the publication date is taken from a Malpedia reference entry [S1][S3].

diamond.adversary: Suspected Russia-aligned, unattributed cluster tracked as UNK_AcademicFlare [S2].
diamond.capability: Device code phishing with a OneDrive-spoofing lure and compromised sender accounts [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Cloudflare Worker URL hosting the spoofed OneDrive page; compromised government and military email accounts used for contact [S2][S3]. Specific domains and IP addresses were not obtained.
diamond.victim: Government, think tank, higher education, and transportation organizations in the U.S. and Europe, including Russia-focused specialists and Ukrainian government and energy organizations [S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Russia and Ukraine themed lures point to interest in Russia-Ukraine policy and analysis [S2][S3].
diamond.technology: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID OAuth device authorization flow; Cloudflare Workers; email [S2][S3].

gaps: Proofpoint's primary report could not be opened (fetch tools failed); all details come from press and Malpedia summaries [S1].
No indicators of compromise (domains, Worker URLs, sender accounts) were obtained.
No sponsor, unit, or government attribution is stated; the Russia alignment is a vendor assessment only.
Exact publication dates for the press coverage were not confirmed beyond December 2025.
Whether other vendors track overlapping activity under a different name was not established.
Number of victims and any confirmed successful compromises are unknown.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Operational environment: Microsoft 365 tenants of government, military-adjacent, academic and think tank personnel are the exposed terrain, reached through the device authorization flow rather than a software flaw [S2]. Threat evaluation: the cluster is a suspected Russia-aligned, low-confidence collection actor using compromised official accounts to gain trust [S2][S3]. MLCOA: continued rapport-building email to Russia and Ukraine subject-matter specialists, ending in a device code prompt [S2]. MDCOA (analyst judgment): use of a compromised military or government sender against defense-linked staff to reach mailbox contents. Candidate indicators: unexpected device code sign-ins, OneDrive-style links resolving to Cloudflare Workers domains, and meeting or interview requests from known accounts that are out of character [S2][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: share the device code technique and Cloudflare Worker lure pattern with unit cyber defenders and mission owners who communicate with academia and think tanks [S2][S3]. Authorities: any Conditional Access change to block device code flow falls to the tenant owner or system authorizing official and should be coordinated through the DODIN operations chain [S2]. Mission assurance: review sign-in logs for device code grants and protect mailboxes that hold operational planning traffic. Coordination: report suspected compromised sender accounts to the owning organization and the supporting cyber defense service provider.
